name: Kubernetes
certifications: KCNA: Kubernetes and Cloud Native Associate

beginner.summary: For people who know basic Linux and have run a container. Covers the Kubernetes objects needed to deploy, expose, configure and troubleshoot an application.
prerequisites: Basic Linux command line (files, processes, editing YAML)
Has built or run a Docker container
Laptop able to run Docker and a local cluster such as kind or minikube
outcomes: Explain the Kubernetes architecture and how the control plane reconciles desired state
Deploy, scale, update and roll back applications with Deployments
Expose applications with Services and Ingress and configure them with ConfigMaps and Secrets
Diagnose common pod failures with kubectl

days.topic: Kubernetes Architecture and Local Cluster Setup
subtopics: Control plane: API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager
Worker nodes: kubelet, kube-proxy, container runtime
Creating a local cluster with kind
days.lab_task: Create a three-node kind cluster, list its nodes and system pods, and draw how a kubectl apply request travels through the control plane.
days.deliverable: Cluster creation transcript, node list and an annotated architecture diagram
checks: Shows one control-plane node and two workers in Ready state
Delete a kube-system pod managed by a DaemonSet
Request path from kubectl to etcd and back to the kubelet is correct
objectives: Describe each control plane and node component
Run a local cluster and switch contexts

days.lab_task: Write a pod with an init container that waits for a file and a sidecar that tails the main container's log, then inspect each container's logs and states.
days.deliverable: Pod manifest and kubectl outputs for each container
checks: Apply the pod before the file exists
Pod stays in Init until the file is created
Shows the main container's log lines
Make the main container exit with an error
Restart count increases under restartPolicy Always

subtopics: Rolling update strategy: maxSurge and maxUnavailable
days.lab_task: Deploy a web app with 4 replicas, roll out a new image version while a load loop runs, then roll back a broken version.
days.deliverable: Deployment manifest, rollout history and the load loop log
checks: Update the image during the load loop
No failed requests during the rollout
Rollout stalls and old pods keep serving

subtopics: Why pods need a stable address
Debugging a Service with no endpoints
days.lab_task: Expose the web app with a ClusterIP Service, reach it by DNS name from another pod, then break the selector and fix it using the endpoint list.
days.deliverable: Service manifests, DNS test output and the debugging notes
checks: curl the Service DNS name from a test pod
Change the Service selector to a wrong label
Endpoints list becomes empty and requests fail

subtopics: Why Secrets are not encrypted by default
days.lab_task: Move the app's settings into a ConfigMap and its database password into a Secret, mount the settings as a file, and update a setting without rebuilding the image.
days.deliverable: ConfigMap, Secret and Deployment manifests with before and after app output
checks: Read the setting inside the pod
File inside the pod updates within about a minute
Participant explains why base64 is not encryption
objectives: Explain the security limits of Secrets

days.lab_task: Create dev and test namespaces with a resource quota on test, deploy the app to both, and delete only the test resources using labels.
days.deliverable: Namespace, quota and LimitRange manifests with the quota test results
checks: Deploy more replicas than the test quota allows
Extra pods are rejected with a quota error
Create a pod without limits in test
Delete resources by label in test
objectives: Organise workloads with namespaces and labels

subtopics: Mounting a claim in a pod
What happens to data when a pod is deleted
days.lab_task: Run a database pod with a PersistentVolumeClaim, write data, delete the pod, and show the data survives in the replacement pod.
days.deliverable: Claim and Deployment manifests with the data persistence test
checks: New pod starts and the data is still there
Data is lost, and the participant explains why
Dynamically provisioned volume is bound to the claim
objectives: Choose access modes and reclaim policies

subtopics: When a Deployment is not enough
DaemonSets for one pod per node
days.lab_task: Run a three-member Redis StatefulSet with stable names and its own volume per pod, and a log-collector DaemonSet on every worker node.
days.deliverable: StatefulSet and DaemonSet manifests with identity and placement evidence
checks: Replacement keeps the name redis-1 and its volume
Resolve redis-0 through the headless Service
Add a worker node to the kind cluster
DaemonSet starts a pod on it

subtopics: Cleaning up finished Jobs with TTL
days.lab_task: Run a Job that processes 10 work items with 3 in parallel, and a CronJob that backs up a ConfigMap every 5 minutes without overlapping runs.
days.deliverable: Job and CronJob manifests with run histories
checks: 10 completions with at most 3 pods at once
Job retries up to backoffLimit and reports failure
Make the CronJob run longer than its schedule
No overlapping runs with concurrencyPolicy Forbid

days.lab_task: Install ingress-nginx and route app.local to the web app and api.local/v1 to an API service, with TLS using a self-signed certificate.
days.deliverable: Ingress manifests, certificate Secret and curl test results

days.lab_task: Add liveness, readiness and startup probes to the web app, then show a hung pod being restarted and a not-ready pod being removed from the Service.
days.deliverable: Updated Deployment and event logs for both failures
checks: Make the app stop answering on /healthz
Pod is removed from Service endpoints but not restarted
objectives: Explain how probes drive restarts and traffic

days.lab_task: Set requests and limits for the app, cause an OOMKill, spread replicas across nodes with anti-affinity, and fix a Pending pod caused by a taint.
days.deliverable: Manifests and evidence for each scheduling scenario
checks: Allocate more memory than the limit
No two replicas on the same node
Taint a node and deploy without a toleration
Pod is Pending with a taint message, then schedules after adding the toleration
objectives: Size containers with requests and limits
Control placement with affinity and taints

days.lab_task: Configure an HPA for the web app between 2 and 10 replicas at 60% CPU, generate load, and record the scale-up and scale-down timeline.
days.deliverable: HPA manifest and the scaling timeline
checks: Run the load test for 5 minutes
Replicas return to 2 after the stabilisation window
Remove CPU requests from the Deployment
HPA cannot calculate utilisation, and the participant explains why

days.lab_task: Package the web app, its Service, Ingress and ConfigMap as a Helm chart with dev and prod values files, install both, and roll back a bad upgrade.
days.deliverable: Chart folder, two values files and release history
checks: Install with dev and prod values
Each release has the expected replicas and host name
Upgrade fails and helm rollback restores the release
objectives: Package Kubernetes apps as Helm charts

days.topic: Role-Based Access Control and Service Accounts
days.lab_task: Give a developer service account read-only access to the dev namespace and a CI service account permission to update Deployments only, and verify both with can-i.
days.deliverable: Role, binding and service account manifests with can-i results
checks: can-i delete pods as the developer
CI account updates the Deployment image
objectives: Use service accounts for workloads and automation

days.lab_task: Apply default-deny to the app namespace, then allow only the frontend to call the API and the API to call the database, keeping DNS working.
days.deliverable: Network policy manifests and a connectivity test matrix
checks: API resolves the database DNS name
Works because DNS egress is allowed
objectives: Restrict pod traffic with network policies

days.topic: Observing a Cluster: Logs, Events and Metrics
days.lab_task: Install kube-prometheus-stack, build a dashboard for the web app showing requests, CPU, memory and restarts, and alert when a pod restarts more than 3 times in 10 minutes.
days.deliverable: Dashboard JSON, alert rule and a fired alert screenshot
checks: Crash the app 4 times in 10 minutes
Open the dashboard during the load test
Read previous container logs after a crash
Shows the crashing container's last lines
objectives: Collect metrics and logs from a cluster

days.lab_task: Fix six broken deployments prepared by the trainer, each with a different fault, using the checklist, and record cause, evidence and fix for each.
days.deliverable: Troubleshooting log with cause, evidence and fix for all six faults
checks: Fix all six faults within the time limit
Read the log for the ImagePullBackOff fault
Cause and evidence from events are recorded
Use kubectl debug on a distroless pod
Debug container attaches and the participant runs a network test
objectives: Troubleshoot common pod and network failures
Use events, logs and debug containers

subtopics: Breaking an app into frontend, API and database
days.lab_task: Deploy a three-tier app (React frontend, API, PostgreSQL) with Kustomize base and dev overlay, probes, a claim for the database and Ingress routing.
days.deliverable: Kustomize folder structure, deployed app and a health check of each tier
checks: Open the app through Ingress and create a record
Overlay changes only replicas and host names
objectives: Apply probes, storage and routing together

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: Production-Ready Web Application on Kubernetes
subtopics: Manifests or Helm chart for all tiers
days.lab_task: Deliver a web application on Kubernetes with a Helm chart, TLS ingress, persistent database, probes, resource limits, autoscaling and a dashboard, then demonstrate a failure and recovery.
days.deliverable: Helm chart repository, deployed application, dashboard and a 10-minute demo
checks: Kill a node during the demo
Application stays available and pods reschedule
HPA scales the API and latency stays acceptable
Install the chart in a fresh namespace
Works with only a values file change
objectives: Deliver a production-ready application on Kubernetes
Combine configuration, storage, routing and scaling

intermediate.summary: For people who deploy applications to Kubernetes. Covers cluster administration, security, advanced scheduling, operators, GitOps, service mesh and production operations.
prerequisites: Deploys applications with Deployments, Services, Ingress and Helm
Comfortable with kubectl, YAML and container images
Linux administration basics and networking (IP, DNS, TLS)
outcomes: Install, upgrade, back up and restore a Kubernetes cluster
Secure clusters and workloads with RBAC, admission policies and secrets management
Extend Kubernetes with CRDs and operators and deliver apps with GitOps
Operate workloads with service mesh, observability and capacity planning

subtopics: Cluster prerequisites: swap, kernel modules, container runtime
days.lab_task: Build a three-node cluster on virtual machines with kubeadm and Calico, then drain a worker for maintenance without dropping traffic.
days.deliverable: Build runbook, cluster status and the drain test log
checks: All three nodes Ready on the expected version
Drain a worker during a load loop
Pods move and the load loop has no failures
Expiry dates are shown and explained

days.topic: Cluster Upgrades, etcd Backup and Restore
subtopics: Upgrading the control plane with kubeadm
days.lab_task: Back up etcd, upgrade the cluster one minor version, delete a namespace by mistake, and restore it from the snapshot.
days.deliverable: Upgrade and restore runbook with command logs
checks: Control plane and kubelets on the new version
Restore the snapshot after deleting the namespace
Namespace and its resources are back
Upgrade a kubelet two versions ahead of the API server
Participant explains why skew policy forbids it
objectives: Plan upgrades within the version skew policy

days.lab_task: Trace one request from a pod to a Service and back with tcpdump on both nodes, then replace kube-proxy with Cilium and compare the data path.
days.deliverable: Annotated packet traces and a comparison note
checks: Capture traffic on the source and destination node
Shows the Service IP translated to a pod IP
kube-proxy replacement is enabled and Services work
Participant identifies and fixes external name resolution

subtopics: Gateway API resources: GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute
days.lab_task: Install a Gateway API implementation, issue certificates with cert-manager, and split traffic 90/10 between two app versions with header-based override.
days.deliverable: Gateway resources, certificate status and traffic split evidence
checks: About 90 reach v1 and 10 reach v2
Send a request with the canary header

subtopics: Pod Security Standards: privileged, baseline, restricted
Running as non-root and read-only filesystems
days.lab_task: Enforce the restricted Pod Security Standard on the app namespace, fix the app to comply, and add a Kyverno policy that blocks images from untrusted registries.
days.deliverable: Namespace labels, fixed manifests and Kyverno policy with test results
checks: Deploy a privileged pod in the namespace
Deploy an image from an untrusted registry
Runs as non-root with a read-only root filesystem

days.topic: Secrets Management with External Secrets and Vault
days.lab_task: Store the database password in Vault, sync it into the namespace with External Secrets Operator, rotate it, and show the app picks up the new value.
days.deliverable: Vault configuration, ExternalSecret manifest and rotation evidence
checks: Kubernetes Secret updates within the refresh interval
Search the Git repository for the password
Read the Secret as a non-authorised service account

subtopics: Writing a simple operator with Kopf or kubebuilder
days.lab_task: Write a small operator that watches a Website custom resource and creates a Deployment, Service and Ingress for it, updating status conditions.
days.deliverable: CRD, operator code and a demo of creating, updating and deleting a Website
checks: Deployment, Service and Ingress are created and status shows Ready
Change the replica count in the Website
Deployment is updated by the operator
Finalizer cleans up the child resources

days.lab_task: Manage dev and prod environments of the three-tier app with Argo CD from Git, promote a change from dev to prod by pull request, and show drift being corrected.
days.deliverable: GitOps repository structure, Argo CD applications and promotion evidence
checks: Merge a change to the dev folder
Edit a prod Deployment with kubectl
Promote to prod by pull request

subtopics: Traffic shaping with ingress or mesh
days.lab_task: Convert the API Deployment to a Rollout with a 20-50-100 canary and Prometheus error-rate analysis, then release a good and a bad version.
days.deliverable: Rollout and AnalysisTemplate manifests with both release histories
checks: Analysis fails and the rollout aborts

days.lab_task: Install Istio, enforce strict mutual TLS for the app namespace, add retries and a circuit breaker for the API, and allow only the frontend to call it.
days.deliverable: Mesh configuration, Kiali graph and policy test results
checks: Call the API from a pod outside the mesh
Retries hide transient errors and the circuit opens under sustained failure
Call the API from a non-frontend service
objectives: Control traffic with retries and circuit breakers
Judge when a mesh is worth its cost

days.lab_task: Spread the API evenly across zones, protect it with a PodDisruptionBudget during node drains, and give the payment service priority over batch jobs.
days.deliverable: Manifests and evidence for spread, disruption and preemption tests
checks: Scale the API to 6 across 3 zones
PDB keeps the minimum available pods running
Fill the cluster with batch jobs and deploy the payment service
Batch pods are preempted for the higher-priority pods

days.lab_task: Scale a queue worker with KEDA based on queue length, let the cluster add nodes for it, and use VPA recommendations and OpenCost to right-size the namespace.
days.deliverable: Autoscaling configuration, scaling timeline and a right-sizing report with cost impact
checks: Workers and nodes scale up, then back down when empty
Cost per namespace before and after right-sizing
objectives: Autoscale pods on events and nodes on demand

days.topic: Observability at Scale: Prometheus, Loki and Tempo
days.lab_task: Add ServiceMonitors, recording rules, Loki logs and Tempo traces for the three-tier app, and build a Grafana view that jumps from a slow request to its logs and trace.
days.deliverable: Monitoring manifests, dashboards and a correlated investigation screenshot
checks: Trace shows the slow span and links to its logs
objectives: Route alerts to the right team

subtopics: Quotas, limits and network isolation per tenant
days.lab_task: Onboard three teams with an automated template that creates namespaces, quotas, network policies, RBAC and Kyverno policies, and give one team a vcluster.
days.deliverable: Onboarding template, three onboarded tenants and isolation test results
checks: Team A reaches Team B's service
Team C installs a CRD in its vcluster
Works without affecting the host cluster
objectives: Choose between namespaces and virtual clusters

days.topic: Supply Chain Security for Container Images
days.lab_task: Scan and sign the app images in CI, generate SBOMs, and block unsigned or critically vulnerable images from running in the cluster.
days.deliverable: CI configuration, SBOMs and admission test results
checks: Deploy an image with a critical vulnerability

subtopics: Incident response for a compromised pod
days.lab_task: Run kube-bench and fix the top five findings, enable audit logging, and use Falco to detect a shell opened inside a production pod.
days.deliverable: Before and after kube-bench report, audit policy and the Falco alert
checks: Open a shell in a production pod
Search the audit log for the Secret read
Shows the user, time and resource
objectives: Harden clusters against the CIS benchmark

subtopics: What to back up: resources and volumes
Restoring to the same or another cluster
days.lab_task: Schedule Velero backups of the three-tier app including its database volume, destroy the namespace, and restore it into a second cluster within a measured time.
days.deliverable: Backup schedule, restore runbook and the timed recovery report
checks: App works with all records present
Database is flushed before the snapshot

days.topic: Managed Kubernetes: EKS, AKS and GKE Compared
subtopics: What managed control planes take care of
days.lab_task: Deploy the same Helm chart to a managed cluster on two clouds, configure workload identity on each, and compare setup steps, add-ons and monthly cost.
days.deliverable: Terraform or CLI scripts, deployed apps and a comparison table
checks: Open the app on both clouds
Both respond through cloud load balancers
Read cloud storage from a pod on each cloud
Works with workload identity and no keys
Covers setup, upgrades, identity and cost with figures

days.lab_task: Handle four injected platform incidents (node NotReady, expiring certificates, full etcd disk, API latency) using runbooks you write, and complete one post-incident review.
days.deliverable: Four runbooks, incident timelines and one post-incident review
checks: Certificates renewed before expiry with no outage
Includes impact, root cause and owned actions

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: GitOps Platform for Three Teams
days.lab_task: Build a hardened cluster for three teams with automated onboarding, policies, GitOps delivery with canary releases, observability and tested backups, then present it.
days.deliverable: Platform repository, runbooks, dashboards, recovery test and a 15-minute demo
checks: Onboard a fourth team from the template
Team can deploy through GitOps within the stated time
Release a faulty version for one team
Canary aborts and other teams are unaffected
Restore one team's namespace from backup
objectives: Design and build a multi-team Kubernetes platform
Combine security, delivery, observability and recovery

advanced.summary: For engineers who run Kubernetes in production. Covers fleet architecture, multi-cluster networking, deep security, performance engineering, platform engineering and running AI workloads.
prerequisites: Comfortable with GitOps, Helm, RBAC, network policies and observability stacks
CKA level knowledge or equivalent experience
outcomes: Design multi-cluster and multi-region Kubernetes architectures
Run zero-trust security and compliance across a cluster fleet
Engineer performance, reliability and cost at scale with measured results
Build an internal developer platform on Kubernetes and defend its design

days.topic: Fleet Architecture: How Many Clusters and Why
subtopics: Single large cluster versus many small clusters
Cluster per environment, team or region
days.lab_task: Write a cluster topology decision for a company with 30 teams in 3 regions, then create two workload clusters from one management cluster with Cluster API.
days.deliverable: Topology decision record and Cluster API manifests with two running clusters
checks: Create a third cluster by changing one manifest
Cluster appears with the standard baseline
Options, criteria and blast radius trade-offs are explained
Upgrade one workload cluster through Cluster API
Nodes roll to the new version
objectives: Choose a cluster topology with clear trade-offs
Manage cluster lifecycles with Cluster API

days.lab_task: Connect two clusters with Cilium Cluster Mesh, make the API a global service, and show automatic failover to the second cluster when the first cluster's API pods fail.
days.deliverable: Mesh configuration, global service manifests and the failover timeline
checks: Call the global service from cluster A
Requests are served by local pods
Scale cluster A's API to zero
Requests fail over to cluster B
No overlapping pod or service ranges

subtopics: Recovery point and recovery time targets
days.lab_task: Run PostgreSQL with CloudNativePG and a replica cluster in a second region, then simulate region loss, promote the replica and measure recovery point and time.
days.deliverable: Architecture, operator configuration and the measured recovery report
checks: Simulate loss of the primary region
Replica is promoted and the app reconnects
Compare lost writes with the recovery point target
Within target or the gap is explained
Original region becomes primary without data loss

subtopics: Workload identity with SPIFFE and SPIRE
days.lab_task: Issue SPIFFE identities with SPIRE, enforce identity-based authorization between all services, and restrict egress to approved domains only.
days.deliverable: Security architecture, identity configuration and an access test matrix
checks: Call a service with a valid identity but wrong permissions
Resolve and call an unapproved external domain
Check certificate lifetime on a workload

days.topic: Policy as Code and Compliance Across a Fleet
days.lab_task: Map 12 controls to policies, test them in CI, roll them out in audit mode then enforce mode across two clusters, and produce an evidence report.
days.deliverable: Control mapping, policy repository with tests, rollout plan and evidence report
checks: Push a policy that breaks a test
CI fails before the policy reaches a cluster
Violating workloads found in audit were fixed first
objectives: Roll out policies safely across a fleet

subtopics: API server request flow and priority and fairness
Large clusters: object counts and limits
days.lab_task: Load the control plane with kube-burner, find the first bottleneck from metrics, apply API priority and fairness rules to protect critical controllers, and rerun the test.
days.deliverable: Load test reports before and after, with the bottleneck analysis
checks: Bottleneck identified with API and etcd metrics
Run after adding priority and fairness rules
Critical controller requests are not throttled
Within the stated target at the test load
objectives: Load test and monitor the control plane
Protect critical traffic with priority and fairness

days.lab_task: Bring a latency-sensitive service from 400 ms to under 100 ms p99 at the target load by fixing throttling, memory eviction and storage bottlenecks, measuring each change.
days.deliverable: Performance report with each change and its measured effect
checks: p99 under 100 ms at target load
Show throttling metrics before and after
Explain one change that did not help
Measured result explains why it was reverted
objectives: Diagnose CPU, memory, network and storage bottlenecks in pods

days.topic: Reliability Engineering: SLOs and Chaos on Kubernetes
subtopics: Service level indicators for Kubernetes workloads
days.lab_task: Define SLOs for the three-tier app, generate burn-rate alerts, run four Chaos Mesh experiments in a game day, and fix the two biggest weaknesses found.
days.deliverable: SLO definitions, alert rules, game day report and fixes
checks: SLO burn alert fires as designed
Each experiment has hypothesis, result and action

days.lab_task: Cut the cost of a provided cluster by at least 35% while keeping SLOs: right-size requests, change node shapes, use spot nodes for suitable workloads and report cost per team.
days.deliverable: Cost reduction plan, applied changes and before and after reports with SLO evidence
checks: At least 35% lower or the gap is explained
Check SLO dashboards during the change
Workloads on it reschedule without SLO breach
objectives: Report cost per team and per request

days.topic: Platform Engineering: Internal Developer Platform on Kubernetes
days.lab_task: Build a golden path in Backstage that creates a service repository, a Crossplane-managed database and a GitOps deployment in one request, with guardrails applied.
days.deliverable: Template, Crossplane compositions, a created service and a platform scorecard
checks: Create a new service from Backstage
Repository, database and deployment exist and the service responds
Time from request to running service

days.lab_task: Build an operator in Go with kubebuilder that manages a Database custom resource with validation webhooks, conditions, leader election and envtest tests, and add a v2 CRD version.
days.deliverable: Operator repository, tests and an upgrade demo from v1 to v2
checks: Webhook rejects it with a clear message
Upgrade to v2 with existing v1 resources
Existing resources keep working after conversion
objectives: Build operators that are safe to run in production

days.topic: AI and GPU Workloads on Kubernetes
subtopics: GPU sharing: time slicing and MIG
days.lab_task: Serve a model with KServe on GPU nodes with autoscaling, queue training jobs with Kueue fair sharing between two teams, and report GPU utilisation.
days.deliverable: Serving and queue configuration, load test results and a GPU utilisation report
checks: Replicas scale and latency meets the stated target
Submit jobs from both teams beyond capacity
Kueue shares GPUs according to quotas
Shows utilisation per team and idle time
objectives: Serve and scale models on Kubernetes

subtopics: When to run Kubernetes at the edge
Fleet updates with GitOps pull models
Azure Arc and Anthos style management
days.lab_task: Run 5 simulated edge sites on k3s managed by a pull-based GitOps tool, roll an update in waves, and show a disconnected site catching up when it reconnects.
days.deliverable: Edge architecture, fleet configuration and the wave rollout record
checks: Roll an update in two waves
Second wave starts only after the first is healthy
Disconnect a site during the update
Site applies the update after reconnecting
Remote access, secrets and updates are covered

days.topic: Kubernetes Upgrade Strategy for Large Fleets
subtopics: Finding deprecated API use with Pluto
days.lab_task: Plan and run a fleet upgrade: find deprecated APIs with Pluto, fix them, upgrade a canary cluster, then move a workload to a new blue-green cluster with no downtime.
days.deliverable: Upgrade plan, deprecated API report, compatibility matrix and the migration record
checks: Deprecated APIs are listed with locations
All workloads healthy after the upgrade
Move traffic to the new cluster
No failed requests during the cut-over
objectives: Remove deprecated API use before upgrading
Upgrade with canary and blue-green clusters

days.topic: Advanced Troubleshooting of Clusters and Workloads
days.lab_task: Diagnose and fix eight hard failures injected by the trainer, including a failing admission webhook, a stuck namespace and an eviction storm, within a time limit.
days.deliverable: Diagnosis log with symptom, evidence, root cause and fix for each failure
checks: Deployments can be created again and the cause is recorded
Namespace is deleted after resolving the finalizer correctly
Root cause found from node pressure metrics
objectives: Use node-level tools and control plane metrics

days.topic: Securing the Software Delivery Pipeline to Kubernetes
days.lab_task: Generate SLSA provenance for builds, verify it at admission, restrict the GitOps controller's permissions, and run a tabletop of a compromised pipeline.
days.deliverable: Pipeline configuration, admission policies, permission review and tabletop notes
checks: Deploy an image built outside the pipeline
Limited to its namespaces and resource types
Detection, containment and recovery steps are defined
objectives: Secure the path from commit to cluster

days.topic: Observability Architecture for a Cluster Fleet
subtopics: Long-term metrics with Thanos or Mimir
days.lab_task: Design and build central observability for three clusters with Thanos, Loki and Tempo, apply log and trace sampling to meet a cost budget, and show fleet-wide SLO reports.
days.deliverable: Observability architecture, deployment and a cost and coverage report
checks: Query a metric across all clusters
Compare log volume before and after sampling rules
Shows each service's SLO across clusters

subtopics: Detection with audit logs and Falco
Forensic capture of pods and nodes
days.lab_task: Respond to a simulated cluster compromise: detect it, contain the workload, capture evidence, rotate exposed credentials, and present a timeline and hardening plan.
days.deliverable: Incident timeline, evidence package, rotation record and hardening plan
checks: Network isolated and evidence preserved before deletion
Use old service account tokens after rotation
Each attack step has a preventive control

days.topic: Kubernetes Architecture Reviews and Design Trade-offs
subtopics: Reliability, security, cost and operability criteria
days.lab_task: Review another team's platform capstone design, write two architecture decision records for its biggest risks, and present recommendations with cost and risk evidence.
days.deliverable: Review report, two decision records and a 10-minute presentation
checks: Each high risk has evidence and a recommendation
Options, criteria and the reason for the choice are stated
Participant defends it with cost and risk evidence

days.lab_task: Design and build a multi-cluster platform across two regions with zero-trust security, compliance policies, multi-region data, self-service golden paths and a cost model, then defend it to a review board.
days.deliverable: Architecture document, working platform, failover and security test evidence, cost model and a 20-minute review presentation
checks: Services recover within the stated RTO and RPO
Create a service through the golden path
Running in both regions within the target time
objectives: Design and build a multi-cluster production platform
Prove reliability, security and cost with evidence
Defend platform decisions to a review board
